claim: A VPC peering connection enables full bidirectional connectivity between the two VPCs; it is point-to-point and does not support transitive routing.
question: What kind of connectivity does a VPC peering connection give?

values.display: full bidirectional connectivity between the VPCs
point-to-point connectivity

evidence.quote: The first way to connect two VPCs is to use VPC peering. In this setup, a connection enables full bidirectional connectivity between the VPCs. This peering connection is used to route traffic between the VPCs.
VPC peering is point-to-point connectivity, and it does not support [transitive routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/invalid-peering-configurations.html#transitive-peering).

claim: Data transfer over a VPC peering connection that stays within an Availability Zone is free; crossing Availability Zones is charged at the standard in-Region data transfer rates, and peering across Regions is charged the standard inter-Region data transfer rates.
question: When is data transfer over a VPC peering connection free?

values.display: stays within an Availability Zone is free
standard in-region data transfer rates

evidence.quote: All data transfer over a VPC peering connection that stays within an Availability Zone is free. All data transfer over a VPC peering connection that crosses Availability Zones is charged at the standard in-region data transfer rates. If the VPCs are peered across Regions, standard inter-Region data transfer charges will apply.

claim: A full mesh of 100 VPCs with VPC peering takes 4,950 peering connections, using the formula n(n-1)/2 where n is the number of VPCs.
question: How many peering connections does a full mesh of 100 VPCs need?

values.display: 4,950 peering connections

evidence.quote: For example, if you have 100 VPCs and you want to setup a full mesh peering between them, it will take 4,950 peering connections [`n(n-1)/2`] where `n` is the total number of VPCs.

note: Derived by the whitepaper formula; shown here as the whitepaper states it.

claim: With VPC peering, on-premises connectivity (VPN or Direct Connect) must be made to each VPC, because resources in a VPC cannot reach on-premises using the hybrid connectivity of a peered VPC.
question: Can a peered VPC use the other VPC's VPN or Direct Connect link to reach on-premises?

values.display: on-premises connectivity (VPN and/or Direct Connect) must be made to each VPC

evidence.quote: If you are using VPC peering, on-premises connectivity (VPN and/or Direct Connect) must be made to each VPC. Resources in a VPC cannot reach on-premises using the hybrid connectivity of a peered VPC, as shown in the preceding figure.

claim: The whitepaper says VPC peering is best used when resources in one VPC must communicate with resources in another, the environment of both VPCs is controlled and secured, and fewer than 10 VPCs need to be connected so each connection can be managed individually.
question: When does the whitepaper recommend VPC peering?

values.display: the number of VPCs to be connected is less than 10
environment of both VPCs is controlled and secured

evidence.quote: VPC peering is best used when resources in one VPC must communicate with resources in another VPC, the environment of both VPCs is controlled and secured, and the number of VPCs to be connected is less than 10 (to allow for the individual management of each connection).

claim: VPC peering offers the lowest overall cost and highest aggregate performance compared with the other options for inter-VPC connectivity.
question: Which inter-VPC option has the lowest overall cost and highest aggregate performance?

values.display: lowest overall cost and highest aggregate performance

evidence.quote: VPC peering offers the lowest overall cost and highest aggregate performance when compared to other options for inter-VPC connectivity.

claim: To let all VPCs talk to each other with VPC peering you need 1:1 peering connections between each pair; alternatively you can use AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN as a network transit hub.
question: What can replace a full mesh of 1:1 peering connections?

values.display: create 1:1 VPC peering connections between each of them
AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN to act as a network transit hub

evidence.quote: Amazon VPCs do not support transitive peering, meaning that you can’t communicate two VPCs that are not directly peered using a third VPC as transit. If you want all of your VPCs to communicate with each other using VPC peering, you will need to create 1:1 VPC peering connections between each of them. Alternatively, you can use AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN to act as a network transit hub.

claim: In the many-to-many pattern traffic between each pair of VPCs is managed individually; in the hub-and-spoke pattern all inter-VPC traffic flows through a central resource that routes it by established rules.
question: What is the difference between many-to-many and hub-and-spoke VPC connectivity?

values.display: many-to-many approach
all inter-VPC traffic flows through a central resource

evidence.quote: In the many-to-many approach, the traffic between each VPC is managed individually between each VPC. In the hub-and-spoke model, all inter-VPC traffic flows through a central resource, which routes traffic based on established rules.

claim: AWS advises giving each VPC a single, contiguous, non-overlapping CIDR block, because VPC-to-VPC connectivity works best with non-overlapping IP ranges for the VPCs being connected.
question: What CIDR planning does AWS advise before connecting VPCs?

values.display: non-overlapping IP ranges for each VPC being connected
single, contiguous, non-overlapping CIDR block

evidence.quote: VPC connectivity between VPCs is best achieved when using non-overlapping IP ranges for each VPC being connected. For example, if you’d like to connect multiple VPCs, make sure each VPC is configured with unique Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) ranges. Therefore, we advise you to allocate a single, contiguous, non-overlapping CIDR block to be used by each VPC.

claim: Use AWS PrivateLink for a client/server setup where consumer VPCs need unidirectional access to a specific service: only clients in the consumer VPC can initiate a connection, and it also suits VPCs with overlapping IP addresses because the endpoint network interfaces sit in the client VPC.
question: When should you choose PrivateLink over peering or a transit gateway?

values.display: Only the clients with access in the consumer VPC can initiate a connection
overlapping IP addresses

evidence.quote: Only the clients with access in the consumer VPC can initiate a connection to the service in the service provider VPC or AWS service. This is also a good option when client and servers in the two VPCs have overlapping IP addresses because AWS PrivateLink uses ENIs within the client VPC in a manner that ensures that are no IP conflicts with the service provider. You can access AWS PrivateLink endpoints over VPC peering, VPN, Transit Gateway, Cloud WAN, and AWS Direct Connect.

claim: Use VPC peering and Transit Gateway when you want layer 3 IP connectivity between VPCs, and PrivateLink when you want unidirectional access to a service.
question: Which options give layer 3 IP connectivity between VPCs?

values.display: layer-3 IP connectivity between VPCs

evidence.quote: Use VPC peering and Transit Gateway when you want to enable layer-3 IP connectivity between VPCs.

claim: The whitepaper says an architecture usually mixes these technologies: PrivateLink for API-style client-server connectivity, VPC peering for direct connectivity or inter-Region needs, and Transit Gateway to simplify connecting VPCs at scale and consolidate hybrid connectivity at the edge.
question: Can PrivateLink, VPC peering and Transit Gateway be combined in one architecture?

values.display: AWS PrivateLink handling API style client-server connectivity
Transit Gateway to simplify connectivity of VPCs at scale

evidence.quote: Your architecture will contain a mix of these technologies in order to fulfill different use cases. All of these services can be combined and operated with each other. For example, AWS PrivateLink handling API style client-server connectivity, VPC peering for handling direct connectivity requirements where placement groups may still be desired within the Region or inter-Region connectivity is needed, and Transit Gateway to simplify connectivity of VPCs at scale as well as edge consolidation for hybrid connectivity.

claim: To use PrivateLink the provider creates a Network Load Balancer for the application and a VPC endpoint service configuration that points to it; the consumer creates an interface endpoint, which puts a network interface with a private IP address in the consumer subnet as the entry point.
question: What does the provider create and what does the consumer create in PrivateLink?

values.display: create a Network Load Balancer for your application in your VPC
creates an interface endpoint to your service

evidence.quote: To use AWS PrivateLink, create a Network Load Balancer for your application in your VPC, and create a VPC endpoint service configuration pointing to that load balancer. A service consumer then creates an interface endpoint to your service. This creates an elastic network interface (ENI) in the consumer subnet with a private IP address that serves as an entry point for traffic destined for the service.

claim: The consumer and the service are not required to be in the same VPC, and when the VPCs differ they can have overlapping IP address ranges.
question: Can the consumer VPC and the provider VPC of a PrivateLink service have overlapping IP address ranges?

values.display: can have overlapping IP address ranges

evidence.quote: The consumer and service are not required to be in the same VPC. If the VPC is different, the consumer and service provider VPCs can have overlapping IP address ranges.

note: Callvale decision (d11-097 c): PrivateLink allows the overlapping 10.20.0.0/16 ranges.

claim: PrivateLink lets a provider privately expose a service in one VPC to consumer VPCs so that only the consumer VPCs initiate connections to the provider VPC.
question: Who can initiate connections in a PrivateLink service?

values.display: only consumer VPCs initiate connections to the service provider VPC

evidence.quote: This allows customers who may want to privately expose a service/application residing in one VPC (service provider) to other VPCs (consumer) within an AWS Region in a way that only consumer VPCs initiate connections to the service provider VPC.

note: Callvale (d11-098): the bank, as consumer, initiates; the sentence says consumer VPCs only initiate connections.

claim: The connectivity-options whitepaper recommends PrivateLink for using services offered by another VPC securely within the AWS network over private IP addresses, and calls it a good solution when the VPCs have overlapping IP addresses.
question: Which connectivity option does the whitepaper call a good fit for VPCs with overlapping IP addresses?

values.display: good solution when the VPCs have overlapped IP addresses

evidence.quote: We recommend this approach if you want to use services offered by another VPC securely within an AWS network, using private IP addresses. Alternatively, AWS PrivateLink is a good solution when the VPCs have overlapped IP addresses.

claim: Interface endpoints are created inside your VPC with elastic network interfaces and IP addresses from your subnets, so VPC security groups can manage network access to the endpoints.
question: How do you control network access to an interface endpoint?

values.display: VPC Security Groups can be used to manage network access to the endpoints

evidence.quote: The interface endpoints are created directly inside of your VPC by using elastic network interfaces and IP addresses in your VPC’s subnets. That means that VPC Security Groups can be used to manage network access to the endpoints.

claim: You cannot attach more than one endpoint policy to an endpoint, but you can modify it at any time; an endpoint policy does not override or replace IAM user policies or service-specific policies such as Amazon S3 bucket policies.
question: How many policies can an endpoint have, and does an endpoint policy replace IAM or bucket policies?

values.display: cannot attach more than one policy to an endpoint
does not override or replace IAM user policies

evidence.quote: You cannot attach more than one policy to an endpoint. However, you can modify an endpoint policy at any time.
An endpoint policy does not override or replace IAM user policies or service-specific policies (such as Amazon S3 bucket policies).

claim: A transit VPC has higher costs for third-party virtual appliances on EC2, limited throughput per VPN connection and extra configuration, management and resiliency work, because you manage high availability and redundancy of the appliance instances.
question: What are the drawbacks of a transit VPC compared with Transit Gateway?

values.display: higher costs for running third-party vendor virtual appliances
additional conﬁguration, management and resiliency overhead

evidence.quote: Transit VPC comes with its own challenges, such as higher costs for running third-party vendor virtual appliances on EC2 based on the instance size/family, limited throughput per VPN connection (up to 1.25 Gbps per VPN tunnel), and additional conﬁguration, management and resiliency overhead (customers are responsible for managing the HA and redundancy of EC2 instances running the third-party vendor virtual appliances).

note: Transit VPC is the older pattern; quoted only as a comparison, not as a recommended design.

claim: In a transit VPC, one central hub VPC connects to every spoke VPC through a VPN connection, and EC2 instances in the hub run software appliances that route traffic over the VPN overlay.
question: How is a transit VPC built?

values.display: one central VPC (the hub VPC) connects with every other VPC
software appliances that route incoming traffic

evidence.quote: In a transit VPC network, one central VPC (the hub VPC) connects with every other VPC (spoke VPC) through a VPN connection typically leveraging BGP over [IPsec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPsec). The central VPC contains [Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/) (Amazon EC2) instances running software appliances that route incoming traffic to their destinations using the VPN overlay.
